scope: Standard 1830 (uploaded RTF) and standard Shikoku 1889 (pinned G1889 reference); pure Python engines and authenticated HTTP backends. Excludes 1846, beginner variants and browser UI.
interpretation: A finite inventory of rule boundaries and observed failure modes, not an enumeration of every possible game state. Each row maps to executable tests whose assertions were reviewed; reference/API replays are labeled integration rather than unit tests.

Reject too few/many players, blank, duplicate and non-string names
Reject reserved, duplicate, empty, non-string and wrong-count player IDs
Caller-supplied IDs, trimmed names and independent nested state
Full board, tile inventory, corporations, homes and token supplies
1889 two-player SIR removal and UTF available only for 4–6 players
Only the lowest-price unsold private can be purchased outright
Offered private must be paid at its current price
Later-company bids exceed face/high bid by at least five
Escrow across companies cannot be spent again; raising reserves only the difference
A sole bid resolves at its bid price, then resumes original seating
Competitive auction starts with the lowest standing bidder
After a pass select lowest remaining bid, even when seating order differs
An unchallenged high bidder cannot withdraw out of turn

Only original, still-active bidders may raise; minimum uses highest live bid
Competitive-auction actor survives JSON round trip
Four full pass cycles force the first private's free purchase
A later unsold private does not discount; bought privates pay income after all pass

Action discovery before and during competitive auction, wrong actor and terminal states is read-only
